sit_001: You can recognise it in October by its crown turning deep brick red, more deeply cut and pointed leaves than a native oak's. It stands by Geleen-Oost railway station.
sit_002: You can recognise it by its dark purple-red leaves and wide, low crown, a few steps from the garden's ash tree. It stands in the Jardin d'Isabelle, Kerkpad, Sittard.
sit_003: You can recognise it in winter by its matt black, hoof-shaped buds, bare while everything else is still in leaf. It stands in the Jardin d'Isabelle, near the copper beech.
sit_004: You can recognise it by its bark, scaly and plated, flaking in irregular patches almost like a plane tree's. It stands on Janskamperstraat, Geleen.
sit_005: You can recognise it by its trunk, four and a half metres round, and a strikingly broad, open crown with room on every side. It stands on Rijksweg Noord, opposite the hospital.
sit_006: You can recognise it by its layered crown, lower branches sweeping down low enough to brush your head, and finely cut leaves. It stands in Sittard's Stadspark.
sit_008: You can recognise it by leaves with a flat, squared-off tip unlike any native tree, and cup-shaped flowers high in the crown from late spring. It stands in Sittard's Stadspark.
